page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes a massive 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 7559 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates ranking in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU throughput and Passmark database operations falling into the average range. Memory performance is robust, showing strong Passmark memory scores and average read/write bandwidths. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates strong to top-tier performance on small LLM inference tasks, but experiences a significant performance drop-off to the bottom 10% when executing text generation on large 70B parameter models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E128-32ads_v7 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, allowing organizations to run large in-memory datasets without paying for excess vCPU compute cores. The inclusion of a substantial 7559 GB local storage allocation provides excellent value for data-intensive operations, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This server is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that require high single-threaded CPU performance alongside massive memory capacity.
